It's ten oh two. Minh is in a meeting. And the phone? On silent.
At the door, Tuan is waiting, air fryer in hand. One call. Two calls... Nothing.
Seventeen more stops are waiting. So the parcel goes back on the bike. And all that's left, is two sad little words. No answer.
We've all been Minh. And we've all felt a little bad for Tuan.
So we built Alodi. An AI agent that rescues failed deliveries, so the second try actually lands.
Here's how it works. Tuan taps one button. No typing. No calling back. And off to the next stop.
From here, Alodi takes over. First, a friendly message to Minh, right away.
An hour later? Still quiet. So Alodi does something lovely. It picks up the phone.
Hi Minh! This is Alodi, your delivery assistant. This call is recorded. When's a good time?
Oh, sorry! Tomorrow after five, please. Leave it with security in Tower B. Or call my wife.
Did you catch all that? Alodi did. When. Where. Who. All in one neat little card.
It checks the rules, then sends the card straight to the next shipper's phone.
And the next evening? No calls. No guessing. Just... delivered.
Minh gets the parcel. The shipper saves a trip. The seller keeps the sale.
Already agreed a new time at the door? Tuan holds the button and says it, in ten seconds. Alodi writes the same card.
And when an answer isn't clear, or a buyer says no? Alodi stops, and asks a person. Because some calls should stay human.
Meanwhile, the hub sees every rescue, live, on one dashboard.
Alodi. Make the second drop land.
